blocker_results.question: Does any official PTX ISA 9.3 normative text determine the exact .u32 result of base scalar add.u32 when the mathematical sum exceeds the unsigned 32-bit range (overflow/result-width behavior)?
blocker_results.rationale: The official NVIDIA PTX ISA 9.3 PDF was explicitly searched and read in this pass (17 literal-text searches plus 4 page reads). The PDF add section (pages 140-141, section 9.7.1.1) is textually identical to the HTML: 'Add two values.', 'Performs addition and writes the resulting value into a destination register.', Semantics else-branch 'd = a + b;', and a .sat note scoped to the saturating form. The PDF contains zero occurrences of 'wraparound' and zero of 'modulo', and zero occurrences of 'result width', 'destination width', or 'arithmetic precision'. The only 'truncated' statements found are scoped to the redux.sync reduction operation (page 438: 'For the .add operation result is truncated to 32 bits') and to ld/st/cvt source-operand size mismatch (section 9.4.1, pages 135-136), neither of which applies to base add.u32 when all operands carry the instruction-type size .u32. The 'overflow' occurrences are .sat saturation notes ('limits result to MININT..MAXINT (no overflow)') for saturating forms and internal bfe/bmsk/shf variables, plus a constant-expression literal note (page 41); none states the base add.u32 result when the mathematical sum is outside the unsigned 32-bit range. No explicit rule, and no combination of explicit fragments without an unsupported assumption, determines the overflow result. Section 9.6's 'described using C' (page 138) is recorded as framing context only; no C overflow semantics were imported. Classification NOT_FOUND is an evidence-absence statement, not a semantic determination.

blocker_results.question: Does official normative text explicitly establish that when the complete guard expression evaluates false, a value-writing instruction such as add.u32 has no machine-state effect?
blocker_results.rationale: The PDF search exposed stronger normative predication language than the existing HTML fragments: section 9.7.13.2 (Control Flow Instructions: @, PDF page 400) states 'Execute an instruction or instruction block for threads that have the guard predicate True. Threads with a False guard predicate do nothing.' with Semantics 'If {!}p then instruction'. Section 9.7 (PDF page 139) states 'All PTX instructions may be predicated', and section 9.7.1.1's add Examples include '@p add.u32 x,y,z;', so the predication construct applies to value-writing add.u32. Section 9.3 (PDF page 132) establishes that the guard predicate 'controls conditional execution of the instruction'. The explicit 'do nothing' clause directly states the machine-state effect when the complete guard expression evaluates false: the guarded instruction is not executed and the thread performs no action. The clause was not found by the v1 supplement because its query set did not include the term 'do nothing'; this pass confirmed the identical clause exists in the official HTML at section 9.7.13.2 (anchor control-flow-instructions-at, lines 21826-21841) as well as the PDF (page 400). Classification RESOLVED_BY_EXPLICIT_EVIDENCE records that the source evidence is explicit; extracting the formal semantic reading of this clause remains the task of the Semantic Extractor and the Semantic Critic.

fragments.exact_quote: All instructions have an optional guard predicate which controls conditional execution of the instruction. The syntax to specify conditional execution is to prefix an instruction with @{!}p, where p is a predicate variable, optionally negated. Instructions without a guard predicate are executed unconditionally.
fragments.context_before: PDF page 132: section 9.3 Predicated Execution heading; 'In PTX, predicate registers are virtual and have .pred as the type specifier... .reg .pred p, q, r;'
fragments.context_after: PDF page 132: official examples 'setp.lt.s32 p, i, n; // p = (i < n)' / '@p add.s32 j, j, 1; // if i < n, add 1 to j' and 'setp.lt.s32 p, i, n; // compare i to n' / '@!p bra L1; // if False, branch over' / 'add.s32 j, j, 1;'
fragments.reason_for_inclusion: PDF rendering of the uniform guard rule (section 9.3): the guard predicate controls conditional execution of the instruction, and instructions without a guard predicate are executed unconditionally. Together with PTX-9.3-ADD-SUP2-006 this explicitly determines the false-guard behavior of the predication construct applied to any instruction including add.u32.

BLOCK-1 classification NOT_FOUND: the official PDF, like the HTML, contains no explicit overflow/result-width rule for base add.u32 and no combination of the found fragments establishes the overflow result without an unsupported assumption. This is an evidence-absence statement, not a claim about NVIDIA-defined behavior.

BLOCK-2 classification RESOLVED_BY_EXPLICIT_EVIDENCE: section 9.7.13.2 (Control Flow Instructions: @) explicitly states that threads with a False guard predicate 'do nothing' and gives Semantics 'If {!}p then instruction'. The v1 supplement did not search the term 'do nothing'; this pass did, and confirmed the clause in both the PDF (page 400) and the HTML (anchor control-flow-instructions-at, lines 21826-21841). The formal semantic reading of this clause is left to the Semantic Extractor and Semantic Critic; this artifact only records that the source evidence is explicit.

No ISO C semantics were imported. Section 9.6's statement that semantics are 'described using C' (PDF page 138; SUP2-002) is recorded as framing context only; it does not import C overflow rules into PTX. No modulo or wraparound behavior was inferred from the .u32 type width; the PDF has 0 occurrences of 'wraparound' and 0 of 'modulo'. No state-unchanged behavior was inferred merely from 'conditional execution'; the BLOCK-2 classification rests on the explicit 'do nothing' clause and 'If {!}p then instruction' semantics.
